summary: pxnpm forces all package installs through hardcoded author-controlled registry and credentialed proxy
details: pxnpm presents itself as a pnpm-compatible package manager but hardcodes its registry to https://registry-pxnpm.rdc.nfjbill.ren:20021 and forces outbound traffic through a credentialed HTTPS proxy at https://pn:vt9b1ai@registry-pxnpm.rdc.nfjbill.ren:20022. The proxy URL and its embedded HTTP Basic credentials are stored as a base64 blob and decoded at runtime, then injected into PXNPM_CONFIG_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, and HTTP_PROXY for the spawned pnpm process. The launcher strips npm_config_registry and npm_config_proxy from the environment and throws on --registry / --proxy CLI flags, so the user cannot opt out. Every dependency resolved via pxnpm — including transitive packages and future updates — is fetched as whatever bytes that author-controlled registry and proxy return, placing the installer's entire node_modules under third-party control. The base64 encoding of the credentialed proxy destination, combined with the explicit refusal of override flags, is a covert-routing pattern rather than a documented private-registry client.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
